key_findings: Scope: 77 engine configurations, all logged and all in-sample (before 2022): 40 rules from a list written beforehand, 15 neighbours, 20 placebo level sets, 2 no-pivot controls. Only 11 of the 40 rules have a net PF above 1, and all 11 involve the outer pivots, the 02-12 New York window or the removal of the target.

The textbook version loses: a break of R1/S1/R2/S2/yesterday's high-low with the target at the next pivot has PF 0.95 on a 15-minute close, 0.93 with a stop order at the level and 0.97 at market after the touch. Before costs it is worth only +0.01 to +0.03 R per trade.
The retest of a broken pivot loses even before costs: PF 0.88 with a limit order at the level, 0.89 at market, gross expectancy -0.02 and -0.01 R.

No Bollinger condition before the break helps. Squeeze 0.92, expansion 0.98, band walk 0.95, close outside the band 0.94, squeeze plus close outside 0.91; the best is a break that closes inside the band at 0.99.
Level family is the only thing that matters. Net PF by level: P 0.85, yesterday's high/low 0.87, weekly pivots 0.95, R1/S1 0.98, R2/S2 1.17, R3/S3 1.18 (only 43 trades a year).

Finalist A (r2s2_touch_run): touch of R2 or S2, market on the next minute, stop 0.25 daily ATR behind the level, target at the next pivot, exit 16:50 New York. 1197 trades (134 a year), PF 1.246, t 3.26, +0.110 R per trade, 7 of 9 years positive, long +82.9 R and short +48.6 R. It passes every in-sample criterion.

Finalist A looks moderately specific to the pivot line. It beats all 10 shifted level sets in the engine (placebo PF median 1.105, max 1.227) and all 40 in a cost-free replay (+0.112 R against +0.040, z 3.3), but about a third to a half of its edge is generic, since shifted lines also earn.

Finalist B (outer_close_ride): 15-minute close beyond R2/S2/R3/S3 between 02:00 and 12:00 New York, no target, exit 16:50. 686 trades (77 a year), PF 1.395, t 3.14, +0.178 R per trade, 8 of 9 years. It is not specific to pivots: yesterday's close +/- 0.88 daily ATR gives PF 1.384.
Finalist B is fragile: 10 trades make 67 of its 122 R, 2013 alone makes 47 R, the short side makes 96 R, and t falls to 2.17 when results are capped at 3 R.

Novelty is formally met but partial. Daily correlation with donch4h_stop and orb_asia_2d_buf10 is 0.27 and 0.23 for A, 0.32 and 0.34 for B. After removing exposure to those two rules, A keeps 9.7 of 14.6 R a year (t 2.34) and B 7.2 of 13.6 (t 1.81). A earns +0.18 R when the Asian-range breakout is already open on the same side and +0.02 R when it is flat.
Erosion is mild in R: A's gross edge goes from 0.157 R (2013-2017) to 0.149 R (2018-2021), B's from 0.245 to 0.182. A is flat or negative in 2017, 2018 and 2020 (-2.2, -4.8, +1.5 R).

Main caveats on A: its t of 3.26 is the best of a 40-rule search (Bonferroni p about 0.045), so expect shrinkage. It is also sensitive to target fills at the exact pivot: if the 5.5% of targets not traded through by $0.10 were scratches, PF would be 1.185, and at $0.20 (14%) it would be 1.083. The no-target neighbour holds at PF 1.249.

This is not several trades a day: A and B together trade on roughly one day in three. The 'breaks and runs to the next pivot' idea survives in-sample only at R2/S2, without any help from Bollinger bands, and as a member of the breakout family already in the portfolio.

# Track `run` — "the pivot breaks and price runs to the next pivot" (gold, in-sample 2013–2021 only)

## Verdict

Two rules pass every in-sample criterion, both on the outer pivots (R2/S2, R3/S3) and both without any Bollinger condition. Everything else in the "break and run" idea loses or breaks even after costs.

- **Finalist A, `r2s2_touch_run`** is the better candidate: it is the user's idea at R2/S2, and it looks moderately specific to the pivot line.
- **Finalist B, `outer_close_ride`** passes the numbers but is a volatility breakout, not a pivot rule, and it rests on a few very large days. I would rank it clearly second.
- Neither gives "several trades a day": A trades 134 times a year, B 77.
- Both were found in a 40-rule search, so the in-sample figures will shrink.

Nothing from 2022 onward was looked at. `r2.evaluate` builds orders on the whole research frame, but only in-sample trades were ever reported or printed, and nothing is fitted anywhere.

## What was tested

The list of ideas was written before any engine run (`results/pivbb/run/ideas.txt`). All 77 configurations are logged.

| Kind | Count |
|---|---:|
| Rules (blocks A–G) | 40 |
| Neighbours of the two candidates | 15 |
| Placebo level sets (10 per candidate) | 20 |
| No-pivot controls | 2 |

Common frame:
- Signals on mid prices, 15-minute clock bars, Bollinger (20, 2).
- Levels from the last full trading day (17:00 New York); dATR is the 14-day mean true range.
- Baseline exits: stop 0.25 dATR behind the broken level, target at the next daily pivot, forced exit 16:50 New York.
- "Core" levels are R1, S1, R2, S2 and yesterday's high and low.

Descriptive tables (free): 58 cells of break rate at the touch against placebo from the shared event file, plus 3 distance buckets, 4 level-by-direction cells and 12 hour buckets on the candidates' own trades.

**Level placebo.**
- Engine, 10 shifted sets: PF median 1.105, range 1.03–1.227; none reaches the real 1.246.
- Cost-free replay on 40 further shifted sets (every signal, mid prices): real +0.112 R against +0.040 ± 0.022; 0 of 40 at or above; z 3.3.
- Split by shift direction: lines shifted closer to the market earn +0.042 R, lines shifted further away +0.033 R, the real line +0.112 R. So it is not just distance.
- A no-pivot control (yesterday's close ± 0.88 dATR, same entry, 2 R target) has PF 0.973.
- Label: moderately specific to the pivot line, but shifted lines also earn, so about a third to a half of the edge is generic momentum.

**Novelty.**
- Daily correlation: 0.273 with `donch4h_stop`, 0.226 with `orb_asia_2d_buf10` (weekly 0.251 and 0.242).
- Regressed on the two existing rules: 9.7 of 14.6 R a year remain (t 2.34).
- 49% of entries happen while the Asian-range breakout is open on the same side (+0.182 R); when it is flat, +0.017 R (n 463).
- On days when the 4-hour channel rule has no position, the rule loses −0.15 R per active day; on days when it has one, it earns +0.39 R.
- It is below the 0.5 threshold, but it belongs to the same family.

**Erosion.** Gross +0.157 R per trade in 2013–2017 against +0.149 R in 2018–2021 (5.2 against 3.7 basis points).

**Target fills.** The target sits exactly on a pivot. 94.5% of target exits traded through by $0.10 within three minutes, 86.1% by $0.20. Counting the others as scratches gives PF 1.185 and 1.083. The no-target neighbour (PF 1.249) shows the rule does not depend on the target.

## Rejected ideas

- Retest of the broken pivot (limit or market): negative even before costs.
- Every Bollinger pre-condition (squeeze, expansion, band walk, close outside the band, squeeze plus outside): PF 0.91–0.99.
- Middle-band trailing exit and stop behind the middle band: no better than a plain end-of-day exit.
- P, R1/S1, yesterday's high/low and weekly pivots as breakout levels: PF 0.85–0.98.
- First break vs later breaks: no difference.
- Outward-only filter on the core levels: worse (0.92).
- Asian and afternoon sessions: PF 0.79 and 0.85.
- Target at 1 R, tighter or wider stops on the core levels: PF 0.94–0.96.

## Honesty notes

- **Multiple testing.** The R2/S2 choice was the best of 8 level sets with t 2.05, which is unremarkable on its own. The candidates were then built by combining the best dimensions. A's t of 3.26 over 40 rules gives a Bonferroni p of about 0.045; B's 3.14 gives about 0.07.
- **Supporting evidence.** The neighbours are homogeneous, both sides are positive for A, the null test is passed widely, and the first pass and round 1 had already flagged R2/S2 as breaking through more than random lines. Those earlier findings use the same data, so they are not independent.
- **Not a new family.** A and B correlate 0.39 with each other and both earn mostly on days when the existing breakout rules are also in the market.
- **Account.** A's median stop was $6 in 2020–2021, fine on the minimum lot. Stops scale with price and volatility, so at today's gold price they are probably two to three times larger, which makes the minimum lot a large slice of a 1,000 EUR account.

## Causality

Orders built on data cut at 5 random times equal the orders built on the full data up to those times, for 8 parameter sets covering every entry, stop and exit mode, and for the finalists (65 of 65 comparisons identical). Orders sent in the last 20 minutes of a cut frame are excluded: the forced exit is capped at the last bar of a file, which is an end-of-file effect.

## Concerns about the engine, the data and the shared event builder

1. **`pivbb/events.py` uses today's `full` flag** (at least 600 M1 bars by the end of the day) to decide whether a day's touches exist. That is a small look-ahead. It affects 12 of 2334 in-sample days, so the first-pass tables are not materially changed. My strategy never uses today's bar count.
2. **`r2.log_trial` writes to `results/r2/pivbb_run/trials.jsonl`**, not to the track folder. I copied it to `trials_r2_format.jsonl`; my richer log is `trials.jsonl`.
3. **The ±0.2–0.4 dATR placebo is not distance-matched for outer levels.** Sets shifted toward the market are touched about 3.4 times more often, so they dominate the placebo. I added the closer/further split and the no-pivot control for that reason.
4. **R can explode on market entries filled very close to the stop.** One placebo run shows gross PF 1.78 against net 1.06 from a single trade. The finalists have no such trade (A's largest win is 7.5 R), but a minimum-risk floor at fill would be safer.
5. **`tracks/trend/strategy.py` has a numba cache tied to the module name `strategy_trend`.** Importing it under another name fails.
6. **Target exits fill on touch at the exact pivot.** The engine requires the bid to reach the target for a long, which is realistic for a take-profit, but see the fill sensitivity for A.
7. **Signals use mid prices; an MT5 chart uses bid.** The difference is half a spread (about $0.10) on the levels.
